questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Going on exchange in Norway allowed me to get visits from home, but also to be closer with family living in Norway. Moreover, I was motivated to go there because of the nature and I found the courses that UIO supplied more interesting than in other universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, since UiO is very good at informing and sending relevant information in advance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The department of social sciences at UiO sent a lot of relevant emails, which helped me a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The SiO Housing organisation was super accesable and as soon as you are registred at UiO you are able to seek for housing. They are also very fast at responding if you have any questions. I lived at Sofienberg Studenthus, which is convenient in terms of how close it is to the city center and parks and nice shops in Grünerløkka. However, the social environment is not that good.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus mean that you will get to explore the city a lot more and still be able to spend a lot of time at campus, since it is a very nice place to both read, go to cafés or other social activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses on master level at Political science varies in length. They usually last 4-5 weeks, and you should therefore be aware that the lectures don't overlap since a lot of the courses have mandatory attendance. However, you don't have to choose 1 course in 1 block. I had two courses at the same time during May, and it worked out fine - as long as they don't overlap.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can registrer for courses at Studentweb. However, the registration proces for master students can vary a bit. I experienced some troubles with it, but UiO was fast to respond at help me out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get all the courses I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure that you understand what the terms are. They differ from course to course. Some of the require a lot active participation and mandatory attendance and others don't. Often the classes are quite small, so it is better to choose a subject that you are interested in since it can be an intimate setting with less students than usual (10-15 students)

Other than that, I think UiO is super easy and provide you with all the help you need.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I followed three master level courses that all had some kind of orientation toward master thesis. In one of them I learned to do a literature review since the exam had this form, and in the others I had to choose a methodology that had relevance for my master thesis. I found this very useful and I felt that the courses had a clear purpose on preparing the students for their master thesis.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was more intimate, personal and also more practical oriented in terms of writing af master thesis but also in terms of labor market skills. Hence, the style was a bit less focused on research and theoretical knowledge, and more on providing the students with actual skills to use in the future. This is different from UCPH in my opinion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Course: STV4031 - Field Research for Political Science

Course: STV4445B - EU and the Nation State - Institutional dynamics and political processes

Course: STV4447 - Education policies in theory and practice - Policymaking in Norway and around the world

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of the three above listed courses, since they all contributed with valuable and new insights, and they were all very well structured. I felt that teachers in all three courses managed to create a safe space and good learning environments.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Norway is a big country, and if you want to explore it you have to either pay a lot for flight tickets to get to the northern parts or train tickets that can be expensive as well. Furthermore, going skiing is also expensive. Especially if you have to rent all the equipment yourself. However, I highly recommend doing so anyways!! But all in all, Norway is just very expensive to live in as a student, but they have many good offers for students that is worth looking into.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Grocery shopping is just very expensive. Especially vegetables, cheese and bread can be very expensive in supermarkets. Alcohol is expensive too - especially at cafés or restaurants.

Also if you plan on being outdoors a lot, the right gear can also be quite expensive, but also worth it (Skiijackets, hiking boots, hiking pants etc.).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It seemed very well developed and fun, but I didn't have the time to engage with them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not use any of these since I did trips and social activities outside of the university. But it seemed to me that a lot of associations and organisations were accesable also for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will recommend renting cross-country skies at SiO Athletica (app. 1300 NOK for the spring season) or at BUA (for free) since it as very easy and fun way to get to see the beautiful nature north of Oslo during the winter (which is long!)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Become a member of "Den Norske Turistforening (DNT)" and book trips to a lot of the remote and cute cabins around the country. Some of them are very well equipped and very affordable.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Being Danish it wasn't that difficult since it very similar cultures.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to learn or speak norwegian - it makes you bond better. Also sports activities can be good.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Norwegians are very kind and helpful, and I enjoyed how much being outdoors is such a big part of many Norwegians everyday life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Choose courses that you find interesting so that you are more motivated to engage in the class discussions as the classes are more intimate
2. Use the campus! It is filled with very nice reading spots and cafés.
3. The level of the courses are pretty similar to those in UCPH, but be prepared that the attendance to a lot of the lectures and seminars are mandatory

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UiO is very helpful and you can most of the times get the help you need

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Becoming so well known with the norwegian nature, culture and language, and also having great experiences with new friends both in Oslo and on trips to other parts of the country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My economy was definitely a challenge during my exchange. It is my experience that it is more difficult as a student going to Norway to get student grants since we get the highest Erasmus grant. I did not get as many grants as I had hoped for, and therefore I had to use all my savings during the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
